title: Cinema
protagonist: Emily Carlin, manager of Majesty Cinemas
primary_metric: opening-weekend (Thursday-Sunday) net profit -- ticket revenue plus concession revenue, minus per-showing exhibition cost -- generated by The Revengers and Lizzie And The Last Unicorn together, comparing which of the two is assigned Majesty Cinemas' single 150-seat theater for all its required showings while the other runs its own required daily minimum only in the 85-seat theaters

options.A: The Unicorn House -- schedule the large 150-seat theater for only Lizzie And The Last Unicorn, opening weekend (Thu-Sun); The Revengers runs only in the 85-seat theaters
options.B: The Revengers House -- schedule the large 150-seat theater for only The Revengers, opening weekend (Thu-Sun); Lizzie And The Last Unicorn runs only in the 85-seat theaters

legacy_conversion_note: The original docx (source/Y2/Session 7/Cinema/Case Study_ Cinema.docx) and its Guide Notes.docx are both fully fictional -- a private theater ('Majesty Cinemas'), a fictional manager (Emily Carlin), and six entirely invented films with invented review scores, running times, and per-showing costs. No claim in the legacy source is a claim about a real theater, a real distributor contract, or real box-office data, so this conversion keeps every Appendix A/B/C figure AS GIVEN FICTIONAL DATA -- the same way a word problem's numbers don't need an external citation -- rather than treating anything as needing sources[]. One correction made during conversion: the legacy docx's Appendix A table lists Lizzie And The Last Unicorn's Audience Review Score as '8.4.1/10', an evident typo (extra decimal segment) in the source table; corrected to '8.4/10' in case.md's Appendix A, consistent with the format of every other row. The legacy Overview/Background (crowds, buttered popcorn, the two upcoming releases, Emily reading a distributor email) is preserved in spirit in case.md's Overview/Background, rewritten to end at the instant of decision per SPEC sec.1.2 and to move the 8-theater/150-seat/85-seat facts (load-bearing for every calculation) out of the Overview and into Background/Appendix C. The Dilemma is unchanged in substance from the legacy docx (schedule the large theater for Lizzie vs. for The Revengers) -- this conversion adds the memorable option labels 'The Unicorn House'/'The Revengers House' per SPEC sec.1.3, which the legacy docx did not have. The legacy Guide Notes.docx's twist (a burst pipe damaging 'two entire theaters', written for an earlier draft of the case with a different theater count than the one the Guide Notes' own author says they later revised the case to) does not fit this case's current 1-large/7-small structure and is explicitly flagged by the guide's own Lessons Learned as something added, then partly walked back, without ever being reconciled with the final stats -- so it is not reused. FACILITATOR.md authors a new twist (a distributor 'flagship placement' marketing co-op fee) built and verified against this conversion's own case.md/case.json numbers instead; see FACILITATOR.md's Twist Soundness Check.

modeling_assumptions.text: D-1 (case.md Appendix D): for the D3-D5 revenue estimate, each of Appendix B's five named attendance windows is treated as one candidate daily showtime slot per movie per theater. The actual minute-by-minute schedule (which may require a movie's required showings to span two theaters at once to satisfy cleaning-turnaround and cadence constraints) is a separate exercise in D1/D2, not required to reconcile exactly with the aggregate D3-D5 revenue estimate.
D-2: a showing's ticket price is the $7.75 matinee rate if its window starts before 4:00 PM, the $11.50 standard rate otherwise -- Appendix B's own stated cutoff, not an invented rule.

D-3: Appendix B's attendance-capacity-by-showtime-start table is used as the modeled fill rate for whichever movie occupies that slot, in either theater size -- the source data itself is not movie-specific.

D-4: four of Appendix B's five concession-spending bands are given as a dollar range; this case uses each band's midpoint as its representative spend. The top band ('more than $40.00') has no stated upper bound, so a representative value of $50.00 is assumed for that band only -- a real, stated estimate, not a given figure, and the case's one genuine flex-worthy assumption (sensitivity_model.py FLEX).

D-5: each major release is modeled running exactly its contractual minimum number of daily showings (never fewer, which would violate the distribution contract; never gratuitously more, since Appendix B gives no film-specific reason to expect above-average turnout for either release).

deliverables.text: A master weekend schedule for all six movies across all eight theaters, showing every showtime and theater assignment, respecting cleaning/turnaround time, contractual minimum daily showings, and each major release's maximum allowed gap between showtimes (Appendix A, B, C).
A daily showing-count table: how many showings of each of the six films run each day (Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun), drawn from the D1 schedule.
A projected opening-weekend ticket-revenue comparison for the two major releases together, under each of Emily's two plans, using Appendix B's attendance-capacity data and ticket prices.
A total-revenue comparison adding a projected concession-revenue figure (using Appendix B's concession-spending distribution as a weighted average) to D3's ticket revenue.

A net-profit recommendation: D4's total revenue minus each major release's per-showing exhibition cost for the weekend, comparing the two plans and stating which Emily should choose, with arithmetic shown.

referenced_from: Challenges (D1-D5 depend on how Appendix B is read)

balance.argument_a: Lizzie And The Last Unicorn only needs 4 daily showings against The Revengers' 5 -- meaning Lizzie never has to run the single worst-attendance slot of the day (the 10:30 AM opening slot, every day of the weekend), while The Revengers, needing 5, is contractually forced to run that weak slot every day, everywhere it plays. Lizzie is also cheaper to be wrong about in the small theaters: at $325 a showing it costs more per showing than Revengers' $220, but it runs one fewer showing a day, all weekend, so its cost exposure per day is smaller than a naive per-showing comparison suggests.
balance.argument_b: The Revengers costs Majesty Cinemas $220 per showing versus Lizzie's $325 -- a real, sizeable gap on every single showing, all weekend, in whichever theater size it's in. The large theater's 150 seats multiply whatever a showing earns; putting the cheaper-to-run film there, at scale, compounds that cost advantage across every day of the weekend rather than only some of it.
balance.margin_basis: Opening-weekend (Thu-Sun) net profit from the two major releases combined, computed per Appendix D's five-slot revenue model: The Unicorn House (Lizzie large, Revengers small) vs. The Revengers House (Revengers large, Lizzie small). See derived{} for the full worked figures and sensitivity_model.py for the runnable arithmetic.
balance.stability: STABLE under a +/-50% flex of the case's one genuine assumption (concession_top_band_estimate, the assumed representative spend for the open-ended 'more than $40' concession band). Flexing it from $50.00 to $25.00 or $75.00 changes both options' totals but leaves the margin at 2.86% and the winner (Option B, The Revengers House) unchanged in both directions -- see sensitivity_model.py. No other PARAMS entry is a stated assumption (all are Appendix A/B/C given data), so Tier 2 probe 5's FLEX[] sweep is limited to this one dial per house doctrine (only assumptions are swept, not cited/given data).

derived._note: Computed by cases/cinema/sensitivity_model.py from case.md's own given Appendix A/B/C data plus Appendix D's stated assumptions; case-readiness should re-derive independently, not just trust this block.

sensitivity_note: A scheduling-and-revenue case with no illness/death/money-stress/family-hardship content -- entirely fictional theater, films, and finances (see legacy_conversion_note). The one real sensitivity is disclosed above and in FACILITATOR.md: the case's single author-estimated number (the open-ended top concession band) does not move the margin or the winner at +/-50%, confirmed by sensitivity_model.py.

cohort_bands.note: Anchors 2-3 run as written; the room typically splits early on review-score vs. cost-per-showing as the 'real' driver (the trap) before D3-D5's arithmetic settles it. D1's master schedule works well as a small-group build (2-3 Heroes per theater) before the group reconvenes to compare.
Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; D1's 8-theater schedule is worked as a shared example for 2-3 theaters (not all 8) before pairs finish the rest independently.

No vote to take -- Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position instead of a cold-call; guide plays devil's advocate directly, defending whichever side the Hero did NOT pick, specifically pushing the review-score/runtime trap to see if the Hero catches that it never enters Appendix B's attendance data.
